title: Meta app secret as a bare 32-character value, with or without a facebook word, or the Instagram app secret boundary
summary: A bare 32-character lowercase hexadecimal value, a 32-character mixed-case alphanumeric value in an environment assignment named for a Facebook app secret, and the same layout under an Instagram app secret name.
rationale: Three rule artifacts treat exactly 32 characters beside a facebook-related word as an application secret, with different alphabets (lowercase hexadecimal, letters and digits, lowercase letters and digits), and each gates on a context word (claim body-length-32-consistency, tool-corroborated, consistency only). No Meta page states a length, alphabet or encoding (alphabet-not-settled, unresolved; format-undocumented), so a 32-character hexadecimal-looking value cannot be attributed to Meta by shape, and the same width and alphabet is common to digests and identifiers. Whether the Instagram app secret shares the grammar is a boundary, not an answer (instagram-app-secret-boundary). The width of appsecret_proof is not asserted (appsecret-proof-encoding). No outcome is asserted.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Whether a bare 32-character value, or one in an environment variable Meta does not name, is a Meta app secret is not stated by any Meta page. Settled by a Meta page, SDK source or changelog that states the App Secret's length and alphabet.

sources.supports: Basic Settings App Secret section states storage and use but no length, alphabet or encoding.
Rule facebook-secret: a context word 'facebook' followed by an assignment-like separator and a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal capture group.
apiSecretPat: a 'facebook' prefix context followed by a word-bounded capture of exactly 32 alphanumeric characters.

Rule np.facebook.1 (Facebook Secret Key): a facebook or fb context word with app/secret/key words, then a word-bounded capture of exactly 32 lowercase alphanumeric characters (case-insensitive flag set).

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. No outcome is asserted. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
